subarrays_with_k_different_integers.brute:

for each start in nums:
    seen = empty set   (rebuilt for every start)
    for each end from start to the end:
        add nums[end] to seen
        if size of seen > k: stop extending this start
        if size of seen == k: count += 1

shortest_subarray_with_sum_at_least_k.brute:
best = +infinity
for each start in nums:
    total = 0
    for each end from start to the end:   (negatives mean no early stop)
        total += nums[end]
        if total >= k and end - start + 1 < best: best = end - start + 1
return best, or -1 if never updated

sliding_window_median.brute:
result = empty list
for each start of a length-k window:
    window = sorted nums[start..start+k)   (sorted from scratch every time)
    if k is odd: append window[k // 2]
    else: append (window[k // 2 - 1] + window[k // 2]) / 2
return result
sliding_window_median.optimal:
small = max-heap (lower half), large = min-heap (upper half), delayed = dict value -> pending removals
small_n = large_n = 0   (live counts, stale values excluded)
prune(heap): while the top is in delayed: delayed[top] -= 1, pop the top
rebalance:
    if small_n > large_n + 1: move the top of small to large, fix the counts, prune small
    else if small_n < large_n: move the top of large to small, fix the counts, prune large
add(x):
    if small is empty or x <= top of small: push x on small, small_n += 1
    else: push x on large, large_n += 1
    rebalance
remove(x):
    delayed[x] += 1
    if x <= top of small: small_n -= 1, prune small if x is its top
    else: large_n -= 1, prune large if x is its top
    rebalance   (balance by live counts, not heap sizes)

add the first k values, result = [median]
for each i from k to the end: add nums[i], remove nums[i - k], append median
return result

basic_calculator.brute:
find_closing(expr, open_at): walk forward from open_at counting depth until it returns to 0
evaluate(expr):
    total = 0, sign = +1, i = 0
    while i < length of expr:
        c = expr[i]
        if c is a digit: read the whole number, total += sign * number, move i past it, continue
        if c == "(":
            close_at = find_closing(expr, i)   (look ahead for the matching ")")
            total += sign * evaluate(expr[i + 1 .. close_at))   (then read the inside again)
            i = close_at
        else if c == "+": sign = +1
        else if c == "-": sign = -1
        i += 1
    return total
return evaluate(s)
basic_calculator.optimal:
result = 0, num = 0, sign = +1
signs = stack holding +1   (sign in effect outside each open parenthesis)
for each c in s followed by "+":   (the extra "+" flushes the last number)
    if c is a digit: num = num * 10 + c
    else if c is "+" or "-":
        result += sign * num
        num = 0
        sign = top of signs if c == "+" else -(top of signs)   (fold the enclosing sign in)
    else if c == "(": push sign
    else if c == ")": pop the top
return result

parsing_a_boolean_expression.brute:
apply_op(op, letters): "!" flips its letter, "&" is "f" if any letter is "f", "|" is "t" if any is "t"
s = expression
while s contains "(":   (collapse one innermost group per round)
    close_at = index of the first ")"
    open_at = index of the last "(" before close_at
    op = s[open_at - 1], letters = s[open_at + 1 .. close_at) split on ","
    value = apply_op(op, letters)
    s = s[.. open_at - 1) + value + s[close_at + 1 ..]   (copies the whole string)
return s == "t"
parsing_a_boolean_expression.optimal:
apply_op(op, letters): "!" flips its letter, "&" is "f" if any letter is "f", "|" is "t" if any is "t"
stack = empty
for each c in expression:
    if c == ",": skip it
    if c != ")": push c, continue
    letters = empty list
    while the top != "(": append the popped top to letters   (this group's operands)
    pop the "("
    op = pop the top
    push apply_op(op, letters)   (the group collapses to one letter)
return the only element on the stack == "t"

create_maximum_number.optimal:
pick(nums, t):   (largest subsequence of length t, monotonic stack)
    drop = size of nums - t, stack = empty
    for each x in nums:
        while drop > 0 and the stack is not empty and top < x: pop the top, drop -= 1
        push x
    return the first t elements of the stack
merge(a, b):
    out = empty, i = j = 0
    while either has digits left:
        take a[i] if the tail a[i..] > the tail b[j..], else take b[j]   (whole tails break ties)
    return out
